title: Deadline and Extraction
premise: Noor Eastwick, a peace-delegation interpreter with a handler's dead-drop number memorized and a go-bag under her bed, receives a meeting invitation from that handler — three days after his body was pulled from the canal. The invitation is either a trap or a test, and walking into it means admitting to the delegation's security chief, Elias Varga, that she was never just an interpreter. As the peace talks collapse on schedule, Noor discovers the network that trained her intends to use the summit's failure to trigger a border war, and the only way out is through: she must expose the network from inside before the checkpoint rosters change at dawn. She burns it down at the cost of her cover, her oldest loyalty, and nearly Elias's trust — and ends the book crossing the border legally, under her own name, for the first time in nine years.
about_author: N. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working high-stakes diplomatic summits across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose professional skill is being believed.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet her mid-interpretation at a fractious pre-summit dinner, fluent in four languages and lying in all of them. That night she checks her go-bag and recites her legend like a prayer. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath polished competence.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. An encrypted message arrives from Handler Kessler's address — he died Tuesday; she saw the report. The invitation names a time, a tram stop, and a phrase only he used. Emotional beat: vertigo; the floor of her double life gives way.

chapters.title: Delegation of the Doomed
chapters.summary: Elias Varga's POV. The security chief audits the delegation's staff and lingers on Noor's file, which is too clean. He distrusts the talks themselves but serves them anyway. Emotional beat: weary duty sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Tram Stop
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She goes, armed with nothing but nerve. Instead of Kessler, a stranger delivers a dead-drop key and a warning: the network knows she read the canal report. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: What Kessler Taught Me
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, intercut memory. Flashbacks to her recruitment at twenty-three: language aptitude weaponized, loyalty framed as family. Emotional beat: grief braided with anger as she realizes how thoroughly she was built.

chapters.title: Clean File, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He runs a quiet background check and finds a gap in Noor's history exactly the width of a training program. He says nothing yet. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. During a plenary session she interprets a delegate's veiled threat and recognizes the network's cadence markers inside official speech — someone else at the table is theirs. Emotional beat: isolation; she is surrounded in a room of allies.

chapters.title: The Second Invitation
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A note in her hotel Bible orders her to sabotage a translation at Friday's session — proof of continued loyalty. If she refuses, the network exposes her; if she obeys, the talks die faster. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Coffee with the Security Chief
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elias corners her gently over coffee; Noor lies beautifully and hates herself for it. Each suspects the other and both need each other. Emotional beat: charged mutual recognition masked as small talk.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She performs a subtle mistranslation — softening one clause — and watches a delegate relax. The network's confirmation signal arrives within the hour. Emotional beat: self-loathing and the cold clarity of survival.

chapters.title: Kessler's Apartment
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Using the dead-drop key, she enters Kessler's flat ahead of the cleaners and finds his private ledger: the network plans to blame the summit's collapse on an 'interpreter incident' — hers. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger Problem
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The ledger implicates a delegate, Deputy Marek Sova, as the network's inside man — but half of it is coded in a cipher only Kessler could read. Emotional beat: hope with a hole in it.

chapters.title: Confession, Partially
chapters.summary: Noor and Elias dual POV. She tells Elias a version of the truth: she was recruited years ago, she's been playing along to map the network. It is true, and it is not all of it. Emotional beat: relief and guilt sharing a chair.

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He decides to trust her — provisionally, instrumentally — and sets terms: no more solo moves. Both know she'll break them. Emotional beat: two liars negotiating honesty.

chapters.title: Sova's Smile
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At a reception she probes Sova in three languages; he answers in the fourth, revealing he knows exactly what she is. Emotional beat: predator recognizing predator across a buffet table.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Rosters
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He learns the border checkpoint shifts change Sunday 06:00 — after that, sealed lists, no movement, no escape windows. The clock becomes physical. Emotional beat: time made audible.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Question
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She stands at her door, bag in hand, one train from vanishing. She unpacks it instead. Emotional beat: choosing the fight over the exit; love against duty begins here.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Burned
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She feeds the network false ledger pages through the drop, buying time and flushing out the courier — a junior delegation staffer she'd mentored. Emotional beat: the cost of tradecraft measured in faces.

chapters.title: The Courier Cries
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She confronts the young courier, who reveals the network's contingency: if the summit limps forward, they detonate the failure themselves — with casualties. Emotional beat: protective fury; stakes become human.

chapters.title: Varga's File on Me
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She breaks into Elias's office and reads his dossier on her — meticulous, damning, and ending with a handwritten note: 'Worth protecting?' Emotional beat: exposed and inexplicably moved.

chapters.title: He Knew First
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He admits he flagged her months ago and let her stay inside as bait without telling her. Trust fractures on both sides. Emotional beat: betrayal symmetrical, forgiveness deferred.

chapters.title: Midnight Translation
chapters.summary: Noor and Elias dual POV. Working through the night on Kessler's cipher, they crack it using a lullaby Kessler once hummed — her mother's melody, his final kindness. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in exhaustion; the cipher yields the network's node list.

chapters.title: Seven Nodes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The decoded list maps seven operatives across the delegation, embassy staff, and border police — including the officer who will hold the Sunday shift. Emotional beat: the scale of it lands; this was never about one interpreter.

chapters.title: Sova Makes His Offer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Sova privately offers her extraction, wealth, and a new name if she lets the operation run — and shows her proof that Elias has already reported her to his own capital. Emotional beat: every loyalty now priced.

chapters.title: Whose Truth
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Confronted, Elias admits the report but insists he filed it marked 'asset, protect.' Noor can't verify it. Emotional beat: love against duty at its sharpest; truth insufficient.

chapters.title: The Delegate Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She confirms the head delegate's chief of staff is the network's true principal — Sova is a decoy. The plan isn't to fail the summit but to stage an assassination blamed on the host nation. Emotional beat: horror escalating past espionage into war-making.

chapters.title: Burning the Legend
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She drafts her real biography — recruitment, missions, the canal — as a sworn statement, destroying her usefulness and her safety in one act. Emotional beat: identity surrendered deliberately; the lie finally set down.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant, Pre-Signed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The network moves first: a warrant for Noor leaks to delegation security, forcing Elias to arrest her or out himself as compromised. He stalls. Emotional beat: duty pulling him toward the unforgivable.

chapters.title: Held
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Detained in a delegation safe room, she talks her guard — a former student of her language classes — into relaying one message to Elias. Emotional beat: caged but not broken; influence as her last weapon.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Door
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias opens her cell instead of signing the transfer order, betting his career on her statement. Emotional beat: duty redefined — loyalty to truth over institution.

chapters.title: Saturday Night
chapters.summary: Noor and Elias dual POV. With hours left, they split the node list between trusted delegates and plan to spring the exposure during the closing plenary — maximum audience, maximum risk. Emotional beat: calm before the storm, tenderness rationed like ammunition.

chapters.title: Closing Plenary
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Interpreting the closing statements, she goes off-script live, inserting the decoded evidence into her translation while the hall's headphones carry it in four languages. Emotional beat: her voice, finally entirely hers, as the weapon.

chapters.title: Chaos in Four Languages
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Delegations erupt; the chief of staff moves to trigger the staged incident; Elias intercepts him physically; the courier flips and corroborates everything. Emotional beat: climax — violence, noise, and Noor keeping interpreting through it because someone must.

chapters.title: The Canal Again
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The chief of staff, cornered, reveals Kessler was killed for trying to warn Noor — the invitation was Kessler's posthumous dead-man switch. Emotional beat: grief completing its arc; the dead man chose her.

chapters.title: Sova Runs
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sova bolts for the border, counting on the old roster. Elias and Noor race the shift change with the evidence packet. Emotional beat: pursuit with the clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They reach the checkpoint minutes before the new, compromised roster takes effect; the outgoing officer, named in the ledger, chooses arrest over complicity and detains Sova. Emotional beat: the system briefly working because individuals choose.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Interpreted
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Inquiries begin; her confession stands; her career as an interpreter is finished and she feels lighter than expected. Elias offers neither absolution nor apology, only partnership. Emotional beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She crosses the border legally, passport stamped, go-bag empty in the overhead rack. She translates for a refugee aid convoy — ordinary words, no lies inside them. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from truth.

chapters.title: What Elias Kept
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He burns his copy of her dossier but keeps one page — the handwritten question — and mails her a letter asking to see her when the inquiries end. Emotional beat: love permitted at last.

chapters.title: Deadline Met
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. Months later, at a small border town market, she meets Elias as the church bells mark the hour Kessler's invitation once named. Somewhere, the network rebuilds elsewhere — but not here, not today. Emotional beat: earned stillness; the bag stays unpacked.
